The unit opened with the agent reviewing the prior results and sizing the work: 4,096 environments, 32 rollout steps, 131,072 samples per iteration, 32,768 samples per minibatch, and 645 trainable parameters. The agent sketched a fused implementation with counter-based Philox random numbers, packed rollout records, warp-level network reductions, GAE, env-grouped permutations, gradient accumulation, global gradient clipping, and Adam.

The agent then wrote the initial solution.py. Its docstring describes one cooperative launch for the whole run, with 256-thread blocks, a cooperative grid sized via the occupancy API, and manual inter-block barriers. The key implementation plan was:

  • Rollout and GAE execute in the same warp-per-environment pass. The kernel stores each sample as a packed 16-byte record.
  • Each epoch shuffles environment IDs and forms each minibatch from all timesteps for a group of 1,024 environments.
  • Four PPO epochs and four minibatches run inside the kernel. Per-warp gradient accumulators flush through shared memory to global gradients; block 0’s first warp applies global norm clipping and Adam.
  • The returned curve contains mean episodic reward per iteration.

Before compiling, the agent noticed a potentially divergent __syncwarp() and removed it. An edit to clean up unused host glue accidentally removed the sp pointer declaration and left an incomplete stream declaration. The agent inspected the damaged host section, restored the sample pointer and argument setup, and then launched the smoke test.

struct SMem {

  float sam[648];     /* Adam 1st moments (block-local replica) */
  float sav[648];     /* Adam 2nd moments (block-local replica) */

The agent worked through a buffer-rotation race before implementing it. With two buffers, a fast block could flush into a buffer while a slower block was still zeroing it. With three buffers, minibatch k flushes into buffer k % 3; after the flush barrier, Adam reads that buffer, while each block zeros buffer (k + 2) % 3. That buffer is prepared well before minibatch k + 2 uses it. The implemented flow was:

const int gb = (iter*16 + ep*4 + mb) % 3;
float* gcur = grads + gb*656;

/* float4 gradient flush into gcur */
gridBarrier(bcnt, bgen, nb);

/* Each block independently clips gradients and updates its shared state. */
...
sm.sam[i] = m2;
sm.sav[i] = v2;
sm.sparams[i] -= stepf * m2 / denom;

float* gz = grads + ((gb + 2) % 3) * 656;
for (int i = tid; i < 656; i += blockDim.x) gz[i] = 0.f;
__syncthreads();

The minibatch boundary still uses a cooperative grid barrier so all gradient atomics are visible before Adam reads them. The releaser-specific barrier and its shared flag were removed.
